advances: Establishes local attainment near positive contact-certified data and a first-order value for fixed marked constraints. Optimized buffered depth involves an additional inverse response for all halfspaces and the motion of the deepest constraints.

proof:
**Fixed-body input.** Apply the predecessor on the full superdifferential of fixed-body marked entropy with the old $P,S,C,L,Y_i$, the volume denominator $M$, and certificate (1). Its logarithmic inequality and sampled equality case apply to the positive old parameters and to the nonnegative integrable limits used below. Its fixed-body expansion is (4) of that predecessor.

**Geometric estimates.** If $g+rB\subset K$ and $d_H(K',K)\le\delta<r$, where $B$ is the Euclidean unit ball, the support-function inequalities about $g$ give
$$
g+(1-\delta/r)(K-g)\subset K'\subset g+(1+\delta/r)(K-g).
\tag{8}
$$
Indeed the support of $K-g$ in any unit direction is at least $r$ and that of $K'-g$ differs by at most $\delta$. These containments give a uniform inner ball at each old interior mark, common positive lower volume bounds and finite upper diameter bounds, and $|K'\triangle K|=O(\delta)$ with old $K$ fixed. Also a nonnegative concave function $U$ on a convex body $K'$ with maximum $m_U$ satisfies $U(X)\ge m_U\,\operatorname{dist}(X,\partial K')/\operatorname{diam}K'$. For $X$ other than a maximizer, extend the line from a maximizer through $X$ to the far boundary and use concavity on that segment. The coefficient of the maximizer is at least the stated distance divided by the diameter. At a maximizer the bound is immediate.

**Touching planes.** Suppose $U$ is positive continuous concave on $C'$ with sampled maximum at most $B_0$. At mark $Y_i$, choose a supergradient $c_i$ of $U(p_i,\cdot)$ at $y_i$. If the ball of radius $r_i$ there lies in $K'_{p_i}$, positivity on that ball gives $\lVert c_i\rVert\le B_0/r_i$ by taking the direction opposite to $c_i$. Set $\phi_i(z)=\max_{X\in K'_z}(U(z,X)-c_i\cdot X)$, so $\phi_i(p_i)=U(Y_i)-c_i\cdot y_i$.

Use 155691fc3768c06f on the lifted fibers
$$
\widehat K_z=\{(X,s):X\in K'_z,\ 0\le s\le U(z,X)\}\subset\mathbb R^{d+1}
$$
and direction $(-c_i,1)/\lVert(-c_i,1)\rVert$ at $p_i$. The lifts are nonempty compact convex. Every anchored combination of points of these lifts belongs to the lift at the anchored base, by compatibility of $K'_z$ and concavity of $U$ on $C'$. Their support values in the displayed direction are $\phi_i(z)/\lVert(-c_i,1)\rVert$. Thus the accepted slope inequality, rescaled by the denominator, gives $\alpha_i\cdot(z-p_i)\ge\phi_i(z)-\phi_i(p_i)$. The right-hand side is uniformly bounded by the bounds on $U,c_i$ and the sampled coordinates. The finite fixed-matrix formulas (3) in the accepted proof give a uniform bound on the rescaled slope $\alpha_i$, since the base and the marked base are fixed. In particular arbitrary affine rank of $P$ and marks at boundary bases are allowed.

The affine function $A_i(z,X)=U(Y_i)+\alpha_i\cdot(z-p_i)+c_i\cdot(X-y_i)$ majorizes $U$ on $S'$ and touches it at $Y_i$. Their minimum $V=\min_i A_i$ majorizes $U$ on $S'$ and equals $U$ at every mark. Every $A_i$ is positive on $S'$ and hence on $C'$. Therefore $V$ is an admissible positive concave parameter whenever $U$ is, and the bounds on the slopes and the coordinates give a uniform bound on the full affine coefficient array.

Use this construction on the old $L$ to obtain $\widetilde L\ge L$ on $S$ with unchanged marked values. The fixed-body certificate inequality and equality case yield $\widetilde L=L$ on $S$. Its positivity on $C$ extends to a neighborhood of $C$ by continuity and compactness.

**Uniform bounds from the marks.** Fix one old certificate and put $d\nu=dm/(ML)$. Let $q_i=d[(\sigma_i/l_i)\rho_i]/d\nu$ for positive rows. Then $q_i\ge0$ and $\sum_i q_i=1$ almost everywhere. In every positive row/fiber pair let $g_{iz}$ be the conditional continuous-coordinate mean of $\rho_i$ on base $z$. Absolute continuity on that fiber puts $g_{iz}$ in its interior, since otherwise the conditional row would be supported on a Lebesgue-null supporting hyperplane. There are finitely many such pairs, so choose $r>0$ with $g_{iz}+rB\subset K_z$ for all of them. Write $\delta=\max_z d_H(K'_z,K_z)$ and $a=\delta/r$. For small $\delta$, the map $T_i(z,X)=(z,(1-a)X+a g_{iz})$ sends each relevant row fiber into $K'_z$ by (8). It preserves the mean in each conditional fiber and hence the full row barycenter $Y_i$. Row Jensen and feasibility imply
$$
\sum_i \int_S q_i(w)\,U(T_iw)\,d\nu(w)
\le \sum_i \frac{\sigma_i b_i}{l_i},
\tag{9}
$$
where the integral for each row is restricted to its positive-mass fibers.

In each $K_z$, fix a closed interior ball $D_z$ of positive volume. For small $\delta$, all images of $D_z$ under the relevant row contractions stay a fixed positive distance from $\partial K'_z$. Indeed a slightly larger ball about the same center is still in $K_z$ and (8) retains it with slightly reduced radius, while the contractions move points by $O(a)$. The chord bound above and the common diameter bound give $U(T_i(z,X))\ge c_z\max_{K'_z}U(z,\cdot)$ on $D_z$ for a fixed $c_z>0$. The left-hand side of (9) is therefore at least $c_z|D_z|\max_{K'_z}U(z,\cdot)/(M\max_S L)$ for each $z$, using $\sum_iq_i=1$. This gives a common upper bound for all sampled maxima of feasible $U$ when $b$ is in a fixed compact subset of the positive orthant. A positive constant competitor and these upper bounds make $H_{C'}(b)$ finite for the nearby families under consideration.

**Compactness and attainment.** The function $\widetilde L$ multiplied by $\min_i b_i/l_i$ is a positive feasible competitor for all close data, and its value tends to zero as $(K'_z,b)\to(K_z,l)$ by (8) and continuity. For feasible functions with objective bounded below, the sampled maxima are also bounded away from zero on every fiber. Otherwise the logarithmic integral on one fiber would tend to minus infinity by its positive lower volume bound, while the contributions of other fibers are bounded above. If the maximum on a fiber is $m_U$, the homothet about a maximizer of factor $1-s$ lies in $\{U\ge s m_U\}$ for $0<s<1$. Consequently
$$
|\{U<s m_U\}|\le [1-(1-s)^d]|K'_z|\le d s|K'_z|.
\tag{10}
$$
The lower bound for the maxima yields $m'\{U<\varepsilon\}\le C_0\varepsilon$ for small $\varepsilon>0$, uniformly in this lower-objective family. In particular the integral of $\log\max(U,\varepsilon)-\log U$ is $O(\varepsilon)$ by integrating the sublevel volumes with measure $ds/s$ from $0$ to $\varepsilon$. The same tail bound gives $\int_A|\log U|\,dm'\le C_1 h(1+|\log h|)$ when $h=m'(A)>0$ is sufficiently small: use the common upper bound and integrate the lesser of $h$ and $C_0e^{-u}$ for the negative logarithmic tail.

Take any sequence $(K_{z,j},b_j)\to(K_z,l)$ and feasible $U_j$ with objective within $o(1)$ of the corresponding supremum. Replace $U_j$ by its touching envelope $V_j$; it remains feasible and within the same gap. Pass to a subsequence along which its bounded affine coefficient array converges. Its limit $V$ is a finite minimum of affine functions, and convergence is uniform on fixed bounded subsets of the ambient space. The bound on slopes, the fiber Hausdorff convergence, and $V_j>0$ on $S_j$ give $V\ge0$ on $S$, hence on $C$. The same uniform bounds and Hausdorff convergence show that the maxima of $V_j$ on corresponding fibers converge to those of $V$. In particular the maxima of $V$ are positive, so the chord bound makes $V$ positive on each sampled fiber interior. It obeys the old marked bounds.

For a fixed $\varepsilon>0$, the integral of $\log\max(V_j,\varepsilon)$ against $dm_j$ converges to that of $\log\max(V,\varepsilon)$ against $dm$, by uniform convergence on a common bounded region and (8). The uniform $O(\varepsilon)$ truncation estimate applies to the $V_j$ and to $V$, the latter by (10) for nonnegative concave functions with positive fiber maxima. Sending $\varepsilon$ to zero proves convergence of the logarithmic integrals. The comparison competitor gives $\int_S\log V\,dm/M\ge0$. The nonnegative case of the fixed-body certificate inequality and equality case give the reverse inequality and $V=L$ on $S$. Thus every such coefficient subsequence has limiting sampled restriction $L$. This proves $H_{C'}(b)\to0$ and $\sup_{S\cup S_j}|V_j-\widetilde L|\to0$ along any such near-maximizing sequence. For the current sampled set the latter assertion follows by matching points to $S$ within the Hausdorff error and using the uniformly bounded slopes of $V_j$ and $\widetilde L$.

Write $\ell_*=\min_S L>0$. There exists $\eta>0$ such that whenever the data are within $\eta$ of the old data, the envelopes of all feasible competitors of objective within $\eta$ of the supremum are at least $\ell_*/2$ on $S\cup S'$. Otherwise one could take data and gaps tending to zero and violate the convergence just proved. Each affine constituent is at least $\ell_*/2$ there and hence on $C\cup C'$. The uniform slope bound gives a positive floor on a fixed neighborhood of $C$. For fixed sufficiently close data, now take a maximizing sequence with gaps tending to zero. Its bounded envelopes with this uniform floor have a coefficient subsequence converging to a positive feasible envelope, and uniform convergence preserves the optimal integral. This proves positive attainment with the asserted coefficient bounds and floor. Two optimal restrictions on $S'$ must agree almost everywhere by strict logarithmic concavity and feasibility of the arithmetic mean. Continuity upgrades agreement to each closed sampled fiber. The preceding envelope convergence therefore applies to the sampled restriction of every exact optimizer.

**Comparison on the actual signed domains.** For $b(t)\to l$, take the bounded finite-plane maximizers $V_t$ on $C_t$ and $W_t$ on $C$ at the same bounds $b(t)$. Both functions are positive on both hulls for small $t$, by the common neighborhood and Hausdorff convergence. Their unchanged marked values satisfy the constraints on the other hull. Evaluating $V_t$ on $C$ bounds $H_t(b(t))-H_C(b(t))$ above by
$M^{-1}(\int_{S_t}\log V_t\,dm_t-\int_S\log V_t\,dm)$, and evaluating $W_t$ on $C_t$ bounds it below by the corresponding difference for $W_t$. In both differences the common intersection cancels. The two logarithms converge uniformly to $\log\widetilde L$ on $S\cup S_t$ by the floor and uniform sampled convergence. The sum of the fiber symmetric-difference volumes is $O(t)$ by (8), so both replacements by $\log\widetilde L$ have error $o(t)$. This proves (6).

For a fixed fiber, suppress $z$ and put $H(X)=n(X)\cdot(X-o)$ at regular old boundary points. A ball about $o$ bounds $H$ away from zero. For continuous $f$ on a neighborhood of $K$, the oriented shell identity is
$$
\int_K f\,dX-\int_{K(t)} f\,dX
=\int_{\partial K}\int_0^{s_t(X)}
 f(o+(1-r)(X-o))\,H(X)(1-r)^{d-1}\,dr\,dS(X).
\tag{11}
$$
To obtain the Jacobian, a local boundary chart has $d-1$ tangent derivatives scaled by $1-r$, and the radial derivative $-(X-o)$ has normal component of magnitude $H(X)$. Convex-body boundaries have Lipschitz charts and a tangent hyperplane at surface-almost every point. The area formula applies to the signed shell by separating positive and negative $s_t$, since old endpoints index distinct rays and $1-r>0$. For $d=1$ the same identity is the linear substitution at each endpoint with Jacobian $|X-o|$ and counting measure. For negative $s_t$ the integral from $0$ to $s_t$ has negative orientation and describes the added volume. Uniform continuity replaces the inner integrand by $f(X)H(X)$ at cost $o(t)$. Dominated convergence, using $H(X)s_t(X)/t\to v(X)$, then gives the first-order coefficient $\int_{\partial K}f v\,dS$ for old minus current. Apply this to $f(X)=\log\widetilde L(z,X)$, sum over the fibers, and use $\widetilde L=L$ on the old boundaries. Combining (6) with the fixed-body expansion (4) proves (7). The value for the current denominator is exactly $(M/M_t)H_t(b(t))$; by (8), $M_t=M+O(t)$, and (7) is $O(t)$, so the coefficient is unchanged.

statement:
Let $P\subset\mathbb Z^n$ be nonempty and finite, with $n\ge0$ and $P=\operatorname{conv}(P)\cap\mathbb Z^n$. Let $d\ge1$ and let $K_z\subset\mathbb R^d$ be compact convex bodies with nonempty interior for $z\in P$. Put $S=\bigcup_{z\in P}(\{z\}\times K_z)$ and $C=\operatorname{conv}S$, and assume $C\cap(\{z\}\times\mathbb R^d)=\{z\}\times K_z$ for each $z\in P$. All hulls and affine coefficients are relative to $\operatorname{aff}(P)\times\mathbb R^d$. Write $dm=\sum_{z\in P}\delta_z\otimes dX|_{K_z}$ and $M=m(S)$. Let $L$ be positive, continuous, and concave on $C$, with $\int_S\log L\,dm/M=0$. Fix $k\ge1$ marks $Y_i=(p_i,y_i)$ with $p_i\in P$ and $y_i\in\operatorname{int}K_{p_i}$, and write $l_i=L(Y_i)$ and $l=(l_i)_{i=1}^k$.

Assume there is at least one contact certificate. This means weights $\sigma_i\ge0$ with $\sum_i\sigma_i=1$ and, for each $\sigma_i>0$, a probability measure $\rho_i$ on $S$ with
$$
\int_S w\,d\rho_i=Y_i,\qquad
\int_S L\,d\rho_i=l_i,\qquad
\sum_{i:\,\sigma_i>0}\frac{\sigma_i}{l_i}\rho_i=\frac{dm}{ML}.
\tag{1}
$$
Let $\mathcal W$ be the set of all weight vectors of such certificates. For $b\in(0,\infty)^k$, let $H_C(b)$ be the supremum of $M^{-1}\int_S\log U\,dm$ over positive continuous concave functions $U$ on $C$ with $U(Y_i)\le b_i$ for all $i$.

For another compatible family of compact convex bodies $K'_z$ over the same $P$, write $S'$, $C'$, and $dm'$ for the corresponding sampled set, hull, and measure. Retain the same marks and define $H_{C'}(b)$ by the same supremum with domain $C'$ and integral over $S'$ against $dm'/M$, with the fixed old denominator $M$.

There is a fixed function $\widetilde L$, a minimum of at most $k$ affine functions on the relative ambient space, positive on a neighborhood of $C$ and equal to $L$ on $S$. For all families sufficiently close to the old family in maximum fiber Hausdorff distance and all $b$ sufficiently close to $l$, the marks stay interior to their own fibers and $H_{C'}(b)$ is finite and attained. It has a representative that is the minimum of at most $k$ affine functions, whose coefficients are uniformly bounded and whose minimum has a uniform positive floor on $C'$, on $C$, and on a fixed neighborhood of $C$. The maximizing sampled restriction is unique. As $(K'_z,b)\to(K_z,l)$, the optimal value tends to zero, the maximizing restriction converges uniformly on $S'$ to $\widetilde L|_{S'}$, and the bounded finite-plane representatives in the proof converge uniformly to $L$ on $S$.

Let $t\downarrow0$ and let $K_z(t)$ be such compatible bodies with $\max_z d_H(K_z(t),K_z)=O(t)$, using subscript $t$ for the moving objects. For arbitrary $b(t)\to l$ in the positive orthant,
$$
H_t(b(t))
=H_C(b(t))+
\frac{1}{M}\left(\int_{S_t}\log\widetilde L\,dm_t-\int_S\log L\,dm\right)+o(t).
\tag{6}
$$
Suppose in addition that for each $z$ and some fixed $o_z\in\operatorname{int}K_z$, the endpoint on the ray through each $X\in\partial K_z$ changes to $o_z+(1-s_{z,t}(X))(X-o_z)$. Assume $|s_{z,t}|\le Ct$ uniformly and
$s_{z,t}(X)/t\to v_z(X)/(n_z(X)\cdot(X-o_z))$ for surface-almost every $X$, where $n_z$ is the outward unit normal and $v_z$ is a bounded measurable signed inward speed. Use counting measure on the two endpoints for $d=1$. For $b_i(t)=l_i+th_i+o(t)$, with arbitrary $h\in\mathbb R^k$,
$$
H_t(b(t))
=t\left[-\frac1M\sum_{z\in P}\int_{\partial K_z}\log L(z,X)v_z(X)\,dS(X)
+\min_{\sigma\in\mathcal W}\sum_i\frac{\sigma_i h_i}{l_i}\right]+o(t).
\tag{7}
$$
The minimum is attained. Using the current total volume $M_t=m_t(S_t)$ as the denominator gives the same first-order coefficient.
